in_text_mentions: When compared to LPP, epidermal atrophy was slightly more frequent in AD (24.1% vs. 18.3%, p=0.51). Overall, the degrees of inflammation and pigmentary incontinence were less severe (Figure 7). The predominant interface change was focal basal vacuolization along the DEJ, which was present in almost all AD patients (96.4%). In contrast to LPP, lichenoid dermatitis and perifollicular infiltration/fibrosis were only detected in a few patients.

in_text_mentions: te, colour, morphology, and distribution of the lesion, as proposed by the recent global consensus [5]. in_text_mentions: On physical examination, there were numerous well-demarcated, oval, ash-brown macules and patches symmetrically distributed over the back, anterior trunk, arms, and legs (Figures 1–3). Antinuclear antibodies (ANA), DNA-antibodies (Anti-dsDNA), rheumatoid factor (RF), anti-SSA (RO), and anti-SSB (LA) were negative. Histopathological assessment of a 3 mm skin biopsy from the right cheek showed mild orthokeratosis, focal vacuolar alteration of basilar keratinocytes, and a superficial dermal infiltrate of lymphocytes, histocytes, plasma cells, and a few pigmented histocytes, indicating mild interface dermatitis with pigment incontinence (Figure 2). Thus, the diagnosis of erythema dyschromicum perstans was established.

plate_findings.evidence: caption: 'Hyperpigmented, violaceous linear macules and patches on the anterolateral and posterior aspects of the neck, consistent with EDP'; in-text: 'hyperpigmented, gray to light purplish-colored macular lesions of varying sizes'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of the anterolateral neck showing hyperpigmented violaceous linear macules and patches explicitly captioned as consistent with erythema dyschromicum perstans in a disease-focused article. B: Clinical photograph of the posterior neck showing hyperpigmented violaceous macules and patches explicitly captioned as consistent with erythema dyschromicum perstans in a disease-focused article.

panels.figure_caption: Hyperpigmented, violaceous linear macules and patches on the anterolateral and posterior aspects of the neck, consistent with EDP EDP: erythema dyschromicum perstans
in_text_mentions: mplete absence of tear formation. The dryness of her mouth simultaneously progressed, causing the absence of saliva production. The dryness led to gritty eyes, foreign body sensation and irritation, and the dry mouth led to difficulty in chewing food, decreased appetite, weight loss, and recurrent oral infections. For the last two months, she had developed hyperpigmented, gray to light purplish-colored macular lesions of varying sizes involving the entire body and skin folds, sparing the palms, soles, and face as shown in Figures 1, 2, 3. On palpation, the skin was dry at a normal temperature.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Real patient clinical photograph of the dorsal forearms and hands showing violaceous, purplish macules and patches; the caption explicitly states these are consistent with EDP, and the in-text describes gray to light purplish macular lesions, matching the ashy gray macule finding of EDP. B: Real patient clinical photograph of the dorsal forearm and hand showing violaceous, purplish macules and patches; the caption explicitly attributes these lesions to EDP, matching the ashy gray macule finding. C: Real patient clinical photograph of the ventral forearm showing violaceous, purplish macules and patches; the caption explicitly attributes these lesions to EDP, matching the ashy gray macule finding. D: Real patient clinical photograph of the ventral forearm and hand showing violaceous, purplish macules and patches; the caption explicitly attributes these lesions to EDP, matching the ashy gray macule finding.
